originalPromptSet.prompt: Use case: scientific-educational. Independent premium near-realistic botanical atlas teaching illustration, delicate authentic reproductive tissue textures, clear volumetric soft daylight on ivory background. Not cartoon, not flat vector. NO text, labels, numbers, arrows, frames, decorative symbols or people. This is teaching artwork, not an original exam photograph. Square composition. Subject: close view of one spruce (Picea) branch bearing a small cluster of MALE pollen cones, pinkish yellow to tan elongated oval cylindrical compact cones with small densely packed pollen-bearing scales. Branch has SHORT SINGLE needles individually attached all around twig, not long pine needles in bundles. A very fine sparse cloud of tiny yellow pollen dust leaves the cones to the open air. Never draw petals, stamens of a flower, fruit, bees or other insect pollination. The full cone cluster is visible; needles may frame sides naturally.

Not cartoon, not flat vector. NO text, labels, numbers, arrows, frames, decorative symbols or people. This is teaching artwork, not an original exam photograph. Square composition. Subject: enlarged botanical teaching view of ONE YOUNG FEMALE spruce (Picea) seed cone, reddish-green overlapping thin ovuliferous scales arranged helically around central axis, with one small sector gently opened as an anatomical cutaway to reveal TWO tiny pale green ovules on the upper/ad axial surface near base of ONE scale, close to cone axis. The scale remains a scale, no closed carpel wall or ovary enclosing ovules. No mature winged seeds in this young pollination-stage cone, no fruit pulp, no flower petals. A few short individually attached spruce needles frame twig, not pine bundles. Clear young female cone and focal exposed scale.

Use case: scientific-educational. Independent premium near-realistic botanical atlas teaching illustration, delicate authentic reproductive tissue textures, clear volumetric soft daylight on ivory background. Not cartoon, not flat vector. NO text, labels, numbers, arrows, frames, decorative symbols or people. This is teaching artwork, not an original exam photograph. Square composition. Subject: extremely enlarged partial longitudinal cutaway of ONE conifer ovule at pollination and EARLY pollen-tube germination. One pale green oval ovule attached by its basal end at bottom to a small slice of seed-cone scale. A thin intact integument surrounds nucellar tissue, leaving a very narrow micropyle opening at TOP. At the micropylar pollen chamber one tiny golden bisaccate conifer pollen grain, a rounded central body with two smaller air sacs, is visibly resting at the nucellar tip. ONE slender pale pollen tube grows from the pollen grain INTO the upper nucellar tissue, ending after a short inward path, not reaching or fertilizing an egg. Keep the two air sacs clearly attached to the pollen grain, not unrelated round cells. Realistic cellular tissue microtexture, not a flower stigma/style/ovary, no anthers, no arrows, no seed embryo and no finished fertilization. The pollen grain is enlarged relative to whole reproductive cone but physically sits at top opening of this ovule.

Subject: three separate PINUS specimens in a botanical comparison, all on ivory background. LEFT one large mature woody FEMALE pine seed cone with overlapping thick brown scales opened slightly. UPPER RIGHT one much smaller short cluster of soft yellowish-brown MALE pollen cones on a small twig with long pine needles bundled in pairs; this male cluster is visibly smaller than the mature female cone. LOWER RIGHT two separate intact unshelled pine seeds (pine nuts) with hard brown seed coats, and one separate ivory shelled kernel beside them. The seeds are not inside a fleshy fruit and the pine cone is not a fruit. No petals, no invented pods, no written sizes, keep specimens separate and fully visible.
